text: In the wet tests for identification of various cations by precipitation, which transition element cation doesn't belong to group IV in qualitative inorganic analysis?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In qualitative inorganic analysis, cations are divided into different groups based on their precipitation reactions. Group IV cations typically include those that form sulfides or hydroxides that are insoluble in water and dilute acids, but soluble in excess ammonia or sodium hydroxide.

Co${}^{2+}$ (Cobalt)

Ni${}^{2+}$ (Nickel)

Zn${}^{2+}$ (Zinc)

These cations are generally placed in Group IV because they form precipitates with specific reagents used in the separation process.

Fe${}^{3+}$ (Iron), on the other hand, is not typically included in Group IV. It belongs to Group III because it forms insoluble hydroxides that precipitate in the presence of ammonia. 

Thus, the transition element cation that doesn't belong to Group IV is:

Option D  

Fe${}^{3+}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

solution.body:
Seliwanoff 's test is a differentiating test for Ketose
and aldose. This test relies on the principle that the
keto hexose are more rapidly dehydrated to form
5-hydroxy methyl furfural when heated in acidic
medium which on condensation with resorcinol,
Cherry red or brown red coloured complex is
formed rapidly indicating a positive test.

Match List I with List II

  
    
    List I
(Atomic number)
    
    List II
(Block of periodic table)
  

  
    A.
    37
    I.
    p-block
  
  
    B.
    78
    II.
    d-block
  
  
    C.
    52
    III.
    f-block
  
  
    D.
    65
    IV.
    s-block
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A - II, B - IV, C - I, D - III
A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
A - IV, B - II, C - I, D - III
A - I, B - III, C - IV, D - II
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The block of an element is the subshell that receives its last (differentiating) electron.

$Z=37$ (Rb): $[\mathrm{Kr}]5s^{1}$, s-block, so A–IV.

$Z=78$ (Pt): $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^{14}5d^{9}6s^{1}$, d-block, so B–II.

$Z=52$ (Te): $[\mathrm{Kr}]4d^{10}5s^{2}5p^{4}$, p-block, so C–I.

$Z=65$ (Tb): $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^{9}6s^{2}$, f-block, so D–III.

The matching A–IV, B–II, C–I, D–III is given in option (C).

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Some amount of dichloromethane $(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2})$ is added to $671.141\mathrm{mL}$ of chloroform $(\mathrm{CHCl}_{3})$ to prepare $2.6\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{DCM})$. The concentration of $\mathrm{DCM}$ is $___________$ ppm (by mass).

Given :

atomic mass : C = 12

H = 1

Cl = 35.5

density of $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}=1.49\mathrm{g}\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of chloroform $=671.141\text{mL}\times 1.49\text{g mL}^{-1}=1000\text{g}$.

Taking the solution volume as $0.671141\text{L}$, moles of DCM $=2.6\times 10^{-3}\times 0.671141=1.745\times 10^{-3}\text{mol}$.

Molar mass of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ $=12+2(1)+2(35.5)=85\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so mass of DCM $=1.745\times 10^{-3}\times 85=0.1483\text{g}$.

$\text{ppm (by mass)}=\dfrac{0.1483}{1000}\times 10^{6}=148.3\approx 148$

Hence, the answer is 148.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift
